why: The highest-risk surface in this change, and the failure is a LAUNCH one rather than a wrong pixel: resolveVersusConfig THROWS both for an id naming no catalog entry and for a real id whose entry does not support the (players, mode) being started. Both are reachable from stored data alone -- an arena retired between builds, or a two-player map stored before four players were chosen -- so an unvalidated read turns a stale save into a game that will not start.
killedBy: arena ids out of storage cannot crash the launch path replaces a retired arena id with random
sanitizeSetup: arena ids are checked against what is offerable falls back to random for an arena the predicate refuses
sanitizeSetup: arena ids are checked against what is offerable refuses on the (players, mode) actually stored, not on the fallback pair
